name: Dog training and obedience
summary: How expats find dog trainers in Singapore for condo living, leash manners, and reactivity — including AVS-aware expectations and why board-and-train marketing needs careful vetting.
body:
Singapore condo corridors, lifts, and void-deck rules make loose leash skills and quiet alone-time training essential. Trainers offer puppy schools, private obedience, reactivity programmes, and sometimes board-and-train — quality varies widely.

## Match the problem
- Puppy socialisation and toilet routines in small flats
- Leash pulling on crowded park connectors
- Lift/corridor reactivity to other dogs
- Separation distress when both adults work long hours
- Basic cues before pet boarding stays

Group classes are efficient for manners; serious reactivity often needs private behaviour work.

## Methods and ethics
Prefer force-free / evidence-based trainers who can explain plans without guaranteed “fixed in seven days” claims. Ask about equipment (prong/shock tools are a walk-away for many families) and whether they coordinate with vets for pain-related behaviour. Board-and-train should allow visits and written protocols — not a black box.

## How to choose
Watch a class before paying packages. Confirm vaccination requirements, class size, and rain make-ups. For imported dogs still settling post-AVS, allow decompression before intense group settings.

## Practical tip
Train in the environment that fails — condo lobby sessions beat only quiet field work. Film your dog’s triggers for the trainer instead of only describing them.
